draft.title: Managing non-current assets
card: A business may own many non-current assets, such as vehicles, machines and shop fittings. It needs a record of each one.
a list that records each asset's cost, location and depreciation.
The register shows where each asset is and how much of its cost has been written off. This helps the business keep track of its assets and maintain them.
It also shows what each asset is worth on the books and how old it is. This helps a business insure its assets and plan to replace them on time.
draft.remember: An asset register tracks each asset so it can be maintained, insured and replaced.

a.q: What does an asset register record for each non-current asset?
opts: Its cost, location and depreciation
Its sales, customers and profit
Its supplier's debts and payment dates
Its wages, rent and running costs
a.why: An asset register lists details of each asset: what it cost, where it is and its depreciation. Running costs matter to the business, but the register is not a record of them.
a.clue: The register describes the asset itself.

b.q: Tom's Landscaping in Bendigo owns six mowers and two trucks. Which use of its asset register is most direct?
opts: Checking which truck is oldest to plan its replacement
Working out how many customers to visit next week
Deciding what wages to pay its staff this month
Choosing how much stock to order from suppliers
b.why: The register shows each asset's cost and depreciation, so Tom can see which truck is oldest and plan to replace it on time. Customers, wages and stock are not recorded in an asset register.
b.clue: Which job relates to the assets themselves?

b.best: Checking which truck is oldest to plan its replacement

problems.detail: The card defines the register as recording cost, location and depreciation, then says it shows how old each asset is. Age comes from a purchase date the card never lists, and Why (b) implies age can be read from cost and depreciation, which is loose reasoning.

proposal.title: Managing non-current assets
card: A business may own many non-current assets, such as vehicles, machines and shop fittings. It needs a record of each one.
a list that records each asset's cost, date of purchase, location and depreciation.
The location shows where each asset is kept. This helps the business find each asset, check it and maintain it.
The cost and depreciation show what each asset is worth on the books, and the purchase date shows how old it is. This helps the business insure its assets and plan to replace them on time.
proposal.remember: An asset register tracks each asset so it can be maintained, insured and replaced on time.

a.q: Why does a business keep an asset register?
opts: To maintain, insure and replace its assets on time
To record the cash it receives from its customers
To track how much stock it has ready to sell
To list the amounts it owes to its suppliers
a.why: The register records details of each asset the business owns and uses, which helps it maintain, insure and replace them. Stock is held for sale, not for use, so it is not tracked in an asset register.
a.clue: The register is about things the business owns and uses.

b.q: Kerr's Gardening in Bendigo owns six mowers and two trucks. The owner wants to know which truck is oldest. Which register detail tells her?
opts: The date each truck was bought
The place each truck is kept
The price paid for each truck
The wages paid to each truck's driver
b.why: The purchase date shows when each truck was bought, so it shows which is oldest. The price paid shows the cost, not when the truck was bought, and a cheaper truck is not always an older one.
b.clue: Age is about when, not how much.
